answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule.** Each identity must reproduce, within tolerance, a signed behavioural fingerprint (action mix, timing rhythm, counterpart preferences) across successive epochs. A sable signature persists per agent, so resets are detectable. Scoring compares epochs via a stored baseline held in a shared vault. An identity drifting past threshold loses its jetty privileges and must re-earn standing from scratch. An attacker running many clones pays full behavioural-maturation cost per identity and cannot amortise it.
